    C(D) is idempotent complete (Proposition 4.4, Step 1) #

    Write an object M as bPart M ⊞ xPart M. Since there are no nonzero morphisms from an object without copies of X to copies of X, an idempotent on M is triangular, so it splits once idempotents on bPart M and on xPart M split.

    • On an object N without copies of X, ρ is fully faithful; an idempotent ρp splits in the abelian category Rep k I, its image is a retract of the good representation ρN, hence good, hence ρ of an object N' without copies of X, and the splitting lifts.
    • An object all of whose entries are X has endomorphisms the square matrices over k, and an idempotent matrix factors through its rank.

    This replaces the appeal to Krause [Kr, Corollary 4.4] in the manuscript by a direct argument.
